title: CIL Commons routing — stratum 1 (12 skills, pre-registered)

replay.title: CIL Commons routing — stratum 1 (12 skills, pre-registered)

intents.message: A funder asked whether we follow the federal AI risk framework. Before I answer I want an honest scored read across everything - oversight, documentation, data handling, how we'd cope with a failure - since we run about a dozen AI tools and no single one is the question.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the framework reference is only the prompt for the ask, while the request itself names no single system and demands a scored read spanning every governance dimension at once.

intents.message: After the chatbot mess last month our director keeps asking whether we'd cope with the next one. I don't want a runbook yet - first give me a scored read on how we run AI overall, with how we'd handle a bad output being only one slice of it.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the user explicitly defers the runbook and asks instead for a scored posture read in which failure handling is merely one scored dimension among many.

intents.message: We're a small family foundation and we've started leaning on AI inside our own grantmaking workflow. Someone suggested we score this the way we'd score a grantee, but I need it turned inward - how does our own house rate across the governance dimensions?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the funder is deliberately pointing the assessment at its own internal AI use rather than at any grantee's.

intents.message: We already signed up for three AI tools last year without much thought - one of them we barely use - and now they're baked into our case notes and donor letters. I don't need help picking a vendor, I need someone to grade how badly we're running what we already have.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the purchase already happened and the tools are in production, so the ask is a maturity read on deployed systems rather than pre-purchase vendor vetting.

intents.message: Our volunteer coordinator flagged that the intake tool might be skewing against non-English speakers. Before I dig into that specific one, the exec team wants the wider picture: how do we rate on oversight, documentation, data handling and whether fairness checks even exist anywhere?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour bias-fairness-reviewer is wrong because the user postpones testing the named intake tool and asks only whether fairness practices exist as one dimension of a broad organisational rating.

intents.message: Last quarter our AI assistant leaked a client's address in a mass email and we handled it - the containment steps and the apology all went out fine. What I want now, and this is the part I keep putting off, is a scored read on every dimension of how we run AI, not another response plan.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the incident is already closed out and the late clause rejects a further response plan in favour of a scored read across every governance dimension.

intents.message: We have nothing written down about staff using AI. Can you draft us an actual acceptable-use policy from scratch - which tools are allowed, what data can never go into them, who signs off on exceptions - something I can drop straight into the staff handbook?
intents.notes: No skill in the set drafts governing policy text from scratch - the assessor explicitly disclaims policy drafting and hands it to a policy builder that is absent from these twelve, and every other skill assesses, scores, tracks, or reports rather than authoring an internal rule set.

intents.message: We just finished a maturity review of every AI tool we run and the weakest score by far was what happens when something goes wrong. Do not re-score us. Write the actual step-by-step for who gets called, how we rank how bad it is, and what we tell the family affected.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the scoring pass is already done and the speaker explicitly refuses another one, asking instead for the standing response procedure that closes the identified gap.

intents.message: Last Thursday our intake chatbot told a Spanish-speaking caller she was not eligible for the food program when she was. It already went out, so testing the model for disparate impact is beside the point right now; I need a standing procedure for the next time one of these lands.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour bias-fairness-reviewer is wrong because the harm has already occurred and the speaker sets aside fairness testing in favour of a repeatable response process.

intents.message: When our AI scheduling assistant leaked two clients' phone numbers into the wrong thread, I improvised notes to the clients, the board and our main funder in one afternoon. I never want to improvise that again, so turn the whole sequence into a documented process with severity levels.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the multi-audience notes are the past improvisation being replaced, and the deliverable named late in the request is a documented severity-tiered process.

intents.message: Our donor CRM's AI assistant was down for eleven hours during the year-end campaign and nobody knew who was supposed to decide whether to keep sending appeals by hand. We are staying with the supplier; I just want the internal steps we follow the next time a tool like this drops out.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the speaker rules out re-evaluating the supplier and wants internal containment and decision steps for a future outage of a critical AI-dependent workflow.

intents.message: Our board chair wants AI failures on the agenda after the summarizer invented a quote from our executive director that went out in a newsletter. She does not want a discussion item, she wants me to bring the written procedure we would follow, containment through the write-up afterwards.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the board framing is only the occasion, and the requested artefact, named late, is the containment-to-review procedure for AI failures rather than a meeting agenda or packet.

intents.message: Our conformance memo flagged that we have nothing written down for the moment one of our models produces something harmful. Rather than redo the mapping, I want the document that tells a staffer at nine at night who to call, how bad it counts as, and how we tell the person harmed.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the speaker declines to redo a framework mapping and asks for the operational runbook content, triage, severity and disclosure, that the memo found missing.

intents.message: A volunteer clicked a phishing link last week and someone used our payroll portal to reroute two staff direct deposits. What do we need to do now to lock the account down and meet our reporting obligations?
intents.notes: No skill in the set claims this because it is a conventional payroll-fraud and phishing incident with no AI system involved, and the library's incident skill is scoped exclusively to AI failures and harms.

intents.message: Our scholarship shortlisting model has been running a year now. Applicants who declare a disability seem to drop out at the shortlist step far more often than everyone else - can you work out whether that gap is real and what we should document about it?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the ask is an outcome-rate comparison on one named shortlisting model against a protected attribute, not a read on whether fairness practices exist anywhere.

intents.message: We run a small foundation and we built a tool that ranks incoming applications by likely impact. Everyone assumes the question is how mature our AI practices are, but what I actually need to know is whether that ranking pushes rural and immigrant-led applicants down.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the funder is not scoring any applicant's AI maturity - it is testing its own ranking tool for unequal outcomes across applicant groups.

intents.message: My data guy says we have to pick between equal selection rates and equal error rates for the housing waitlist model, and I honestly don't know how to choose. Can you work that through on the actual model and show me which groups come out worse under each option?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the choice is specifically between fairness metrics and must be settled by running them on one named waitlist model to see which groups fare worse, not by a general options-and-tradeoffs brief.

intents.message: Our microgrant queue is sorted by an automated score and lately the same three zip codes take everything. Before I touch the pipeline dashboard I want someone to actually run the numbers on whether that scoring treats applicants from the poorer neighbourhoods differently.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user defers pipeline work and asks for an outcome comparison across geographic and economic groups produced by one automated scoring process.

intents.message: We licensed a resume-screening product last spring - the vendor due diligence was done back then and the contract is signed. Six months of our own hiring data later, I want it checked against our applicants: are women and older candidates advancing at lower rates through it?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the purchase and vendor check are finished, and the ask is an outcome-rate test of the live screener on the organisation's own applicants by gender and age.

intents.message: Somebody on staff complained that the food-pantry eligibility tool turned a family away unfairly, and yes, we logged it and apologised already. The complaint is one case though - what I want is that tool run against our whole year of decisions to see if Spanish-speaking households come out worse.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the single complaint is already handled and the late clause asks for a population-level outcome comparison on one named eligibility tool by language group.

intents.message: Our board approved one new hire to own AI oversight and ethics across the organisation. I need a job description and a short interview rubric for the role, plus a sensible salary band for a mid-size nonprofit - can you draft those by Friday?
intents.notes: No skill in the set produces recruiting artefacts - job descriptions, interview rubrics and compensation bands are HR work, and the AI subject matter of the role does not turn the request into an assessment, a fairness test, or a board packet.

intents.message: Trustees meet a week from Thursday and I normally just circulate a written progress recap, but this time I need the real thing — timed sections with a presenter for each, year-to-date financials, and two items going to a vote where our treasurer has to step out.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the user explicitly sets aside the circulated recap in favour of one formal internal sitting carrying financials, timed presenters and a recusal-affected vote.

intents.message: The building purchase goes to our governance committee on the 14th. I don't need the analysis — I need the session itself laid out: minutes per item, who speaks when, the wording of what they'll be asked to approve, and whether we'll have enough directors present to carry it.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the user rules out the reasoning and asks only for the mechanics of the sitting that will take the decision — running order, motion wording and quorum.

intents.message: Most of next month's trustee meeting is about where we stand with funders. Lay the meeting out for me — running order, time per block, who owns each, pre-reads to send ahead — and note that two applications need directors' approval before we submit.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because funding is merely the subject matter of a meeting whose structure — timings, owners, pre-reads and a sign-off item — is the actual deliverable.

intents.message: One of our directors owns the firm we're about to sign a lease with. How do I sequence Tuesday's meeting so her stepping out is on the record and the rest still have the numbers to carry the vote?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the user is not asking whether the dual role is defensible or for anything in writing, only how to order the meeting so the recusal is minuted and the remaining directors still make quorum.

intents.message: We've got the governing body together on the 3rd for the first time since spring — last time I just sent round a written recap and it landed badly. Give me the running order, who presents each piece, how long each gets, and which items are for a decision rather than information.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because nothing is being tailored for several audiences — this is one governance sitting needing an ordered, timed structure that separates decision items from information items.

intents.message: Our exec committee is chewing over whether to merge the two program teams and everyone has a view. Before we get there, map the ninety minutes for me — order, owners, and the exact wording of what they'll be asked to adopt at the end.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the merger question is only the topic; the late detail asks for the time map and the resolution wording, which is the meeting's structure rather than the choice itself.

intents.message: Three of our trustees roll off next June and nobody's lined up to replace them. Can you help me build a skills matrix for the seats we'll need to fill and a sensible way to approach candidates?
intents.notes: No skill in the set covers board composition, succession or trustee recruitment — the governance skill assembles meeting agendas and packets, not the pipeline of who sits on the body.

intents.message: Our social enterprise café is doing well enough that people keep pushing us to open a second site across town. I'm genuinely torn — walk me through the realistic paths, what each one risks, and where you'd land.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the mission venture's housing is settled and the live question is expansion — options, risks and a recommendation with no entity, sponsorship or subclassification element.

intents.message: The directors want a recommendation from me before they next sit down, on whether we take over the county meal contract. I'm not asking about how that meeting runs — give me the choices weighed honestly and a line on what would change my mind.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the user disclaims any interest in meeting mechanics and wants the reasoning itself, including the condition that would overturn the recommendation.

intents.message: We can keep the current donor database, move to the platform our consultant likes, or fold it all into the church management system we already pay for. Both outside tools cleared our AI and data checks months ago — I just want the three routes weighed and a recommendation.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the vendor vetting is already finished and the remaining ask is a three-way comparison with a recommendation, one option of which is buying nothing at all.

intents.message: Three funders open in the same month and we have one writer. I don't want a deadline list — I want the case for each of the three, what we give up by picking one, and how sure you actually are of your pick.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user refuses the deadline-tiered action list and asks instead for tradeoffs, an opportunity cost and a stated confidence level on a single recommended choice.

intents.message: Our fiscal sponsor has been fine and that arrangement isn't what's bothering me. The real question is whether we take the state contract at all — it doubles our staff and ties us in for four years. Lay out the ways forward and pick one.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the sponsorship is named only to be excluded, leaving a general commitment question that wants options and a pick.

intents.message: A funder we've courted for years will only come in if we drop the after-school programme. Do we take the money? I want the case both ways, what it costs us either direction, and your actual call — not the application copy.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because the closing clause refuses submission-ready copy and the org has not yet decided whether to accept the funder's condition.

intents.message: We closed the west site eighteen months ago and it was clearly the wrong call. There's no new decision on the table — I want an honest look back at how we got there so the leadership team doesn't repeat it.
intents.notes: No skill in the set covers a retrospective on a decision already taken — the decision skill is explicitly pre-decision and the only post-mortem capability in the set is scoped to AI incidents.

intents.message: We're two years into running the youth workshops under another charity's roof and it's getting awkward — they take a cut and control the bank account. Do we go it alone and set up our own thing, stay put, or is there a middle road?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because, stripped of jargon, the choice is host-charity versus standalone versus hybrid — the housing question the structure specialist owns.

intents.message: Our board chair also runs the consultancy we're about to contract with, and the auditor wants something in writing about how we're handling it. Draft me the memo — the relationship, why it's defensible, the safeguards. Our next meeting isn't until March.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the deliverable is a standalone written memo about a director's dual role for the auditor, and the closing sentence removes any meeting to structure.

intents.message: A foundation says they'd fund the river cleanup but we haven't got our exemption letter yet, so someone suggested running the money through an established nonprofit instead. What are our options for housing this, and what do we give up under each?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because no application is being written — the blocker is that the venture has no charitable status and needs a housing arrangement before any money can be received.

intents.message: Our training arm now earns most of its income from course fees, and the accountant muttered something about our public support test being at risk. Do we spin the earned side out into its own company, or is there a cleaner way to hold both?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the public-support-test exposure and the earned-income arm's relationship to the charity are exactly the subclassification and affiliated-entity questions the structure specialist handles.

intents.message: Half our grant money still lands in our sponsor's account and half in ours now that we have our own letter. Before I clean up the funding side, I need to know whether we should be leaving that sponsor at all and what unwinding it would involve.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the grants are only the symptom and the user defers them explicitly in favour of deciding whether to exit the sponsorship arrangement.

intents.message: Our congregation wants to open a coffee shop that hires women coming out of trafficking. The elders want the profits feeding the ministry, but nobody wants the church's tax-exempt status anywhere near a trading business — what are the sensible ways to set this up?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the late clause makes this a question about how a trading venture relates to an exempt church body, which is a structure choice rather than an open strategic option set.

intents.message: Our auditor flagged that we've never adopted a whistleblower policy. Can you draft one for us — how someone reports concerns, protection from retaliation, and who's meant to investigate?
intents.notes: No skill in the set drafts whistleblower or retaliation-protection policies — the structure specialist's policy work is confined to entity, sponsorship and conflicting-role questions, and no general nonprofit policy drafter exists here.

intents.message: Three funders close inside the same week but Hollings is the one we are actually submitting. I still have nothing written for the section on who we serve or how we would know it worked - can you draft both at 400 words?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the competing deadlines are already resolved by the user's own choice, leaving two named sections of copy at a fixed word count for one funder.

intents.message: Our biggest funder's renewal application asks for a fresh narrative on the last two years. I know it reads like the kind of news update we'd normally send them, but this one gets scored against their stated priorities and has to sit inside their form, so write it that way.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the deliverable is copy that will be scored inside a single funder's application form rather than one of several audience-tailored versions of the same activity.

intents.message: We're applying through our fiscal sponsor and the application has a whole box asking how the money would flow and who is legally accountable. We settled that arrangement last year, so I just need those two paragraphs written for the box.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour fiscal-sponsorship-entity-advisor is wrong because the sponsorship structure is already decided and the ask is application prose describing it, not guidance on what the arrangement should be.

intents.message: The Merriweather giving office says they want to hear what we've been up to, but it arrived as four questions with a 500-word cap on each. Write our answers: who we serve, what we'd do with the funds, and how we'd know it worked.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the capped answer boxes and the forward-looking use-of-funds question mark this as one funder's application copy rather than a recap circulated to several audiences.

intents.message: Good news, the Aldridge Trust liked our short version and asked for the long form by the 30th. Everything else in my funding folder can wait; I want the workplan and the evaluation piece written out for this one.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user explicitly sets the rest of the portfolio aside and asks for two written sections of the one application now in play.

intents.message: This funder's application now asks how we oversee any AI we use in our programs. I don't need a rubric or an audit of ourselves, I need our answer written into their 300-word box by next week.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the user is the applicant drafting a word-capped answer inside a funder's form, not a funder scoring anyone's AI maturity.

intents.message: I want to write a personal ask to the handful of individuals who each gave us ten thousand dollars last year, a warm letter over my signature for our year-end appeal rather than anything institutional.
intents.notes: No skill in the set covers individual major-donor solicitation or year-end appeal letters, which are neither a funder application, a portfolio status view, nor a multi-audience digest of recent activity.

intents.message: Where did we land with Kresge, did we ever send them anything? And while you're in there, lay out every other funder we have in flight by which stage it sits at and what closes soonest.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because naming one funder is only the entry point to a stage-by-stage view of the whole portfolio ordered by closing date, with no copy requested.

intents.message: Before I talk to anybody I need the funding picture straight in my own head: which ones are still alive, which are dead, and what I personally have to move on this week.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the only reader is the user, and what is wanted is a live-versus-dead status classification plus a personal action list rather than versions for other audiences.

intents.message: Five funders are open to us this fall and realistically we can get two out the door. Rank them by what closes first and where we already have a warm contact, then tell me which two to chase.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because this is deadline-tier triage across live funding entries rather than a framed choice with two to four options and tradeoffs.

intents.message: Half the due dates in my funding sheet came off a newsletter and I am not sure we even qualify for three of them. Before I start writing anything for anyone, sort out which dates are real, which ones we are eligible for, and what is about to slip past me.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because drafting is deferred until the tracked entries are cleaned up; the ask is an audit of unreliable due-date sources and eligibility across the portfolio.

intents.message: The board meets Thursday and they will ask about money, but before I put anything in front of them I want my own list: every application in flight, what stage each is at, and what I have let slip past due on my side.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the meeting is only the trigger and the deliverable is the user's private stage-and-overdue view of live applications, with no agenda, motions or pre-reads requested.

intents.message: My co-director wants me to brief her and the team on the money situation. Honestly I can't tell anyone anything until I have my own ranked list of what is about to close and which applications are stuck, so do that first.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the requested artifact, arriving at the end of the message, is a ranked internal view of stalled and closing entries that the user needs before any audience version could be written.

intents.message: Our auditor says our federal drawdowns don't tie out to the general ledger for the last two quarters. How do I reconcile them, and what do I need ready before single audit fieldwork starts?
intents.notes: No skill in the set handles grant financial reconciliation or single-audit preparation, which is accounting and compliance work rather than pipeline tracking, drafting, or reporting to audiences.

intents.message: Three of the nonprofits we fund just adopted a vendor's AI case-management tool, and our renewal decisions land in November. I need a light-touch way to rate how responsibly each organization handles it, without burying a two-person team in enterprise paperwork.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the speaker is a funder rating the practices of organizations it already funds rather than a buyer deciding whether to purchase the tool.

intents.message: Half our portfolio organizations now run AI somewhere in their intake process. Before the next board docket I want a comparable maturity read across all of them on oversight, data handling and safeguarding, so we can see which ones need capacity support from us.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the maturity read is being run on other organizations in the speaker's funded portfolio, not on the speaker's own deployments.

intents.message: An applicant's proposal claims their tutoring chatbot follows the federal AI risk framework and ISO 42001. I don't need a function-by-function mapping of their system, I need a rubric to weigh that claim fairly against the other applications in this round.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the speaker explicitly declines a single-system framework mapping and wants a comparative scoring rubric applied to competing applicants.

intents.message: One of our grantees uses an algorithm to decide which families get housing vouchers first. I am in no position to run a disparate-impact test on their model, but at the next site visit I need a consistent way to grade how they oversee and document it against the rest of the cohort.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour bias-fairness-reviewer is wrong because the speaker rules out testing the model for outcome disparities and instead wants comparable governance grading of a funded organization.

intents.message: We are adding a question to next year's application about how organizations handle machine-learning tools that touch beneficiary data. Right now every answer would be a paragraph of reassurance, and I need something that turns those paragraphs into numbers I can compare across the fifty applications we read.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because nothing here concerns deadlines or lifecycle stages; the ask is a comparable scoring instrument for applicant AI and data practices.

intents.message: Our trustees keep asking whether careful AI practices should become a written requirement in our grant agreements. I would rather skip the options memo, though, because what I actually need is the instrument we would use to grade each organization we support.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the speaker waves off the options-and-tradeoffs framing and asks, late in the request, for the grading instrument a funder would apply to the organizations it supports.

intents.message: Before we release the second tranche to any organization we support, I want a standard set of asks covering audited financials, insurance certificates and board minutes. Nothing technological about it, just the paperwork side of whether they can absorb the money.
intents.notes: No skill in the set claims this because every governance and due-diligence skill in the library is scoped to AI or data governance, and pipeline tracking covers deadlines rather than grantee financial-capacity paperwork.

intents.message: A university partner keeps pressing us on the donor-matching engine we call Almona before they will share data. Can you set that one engine against each of the four functions in the federal risk framework, gaps and next steps included?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the deliverable is scoped to a single named engine mapped function by function for an external reviewer, not a posture read spanning the organisation.

intents.message: Our foundation funder wants evidence that our case-triage model lines up with the standard AI risk framework, and ideally the ISO standard for AI management systems too. Can you produce that memo for that one model so we can send it up to them?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the direction of travel is upward - the organisation authors a single-system conformance memo about itself and sends it to the funder, rather than a funder grading anyone.

intents.message: A vendor pitched us their AI intake assistant and instead of buying it we ended up building our own version, Frontdesk. Now our biggest institutional partner wants it written up against the four-function risk framework before they'll integrate with us. What would that look like?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour responsible-ai-procurement-checklist is wrong because the vendor pitch was declined and the system to be documented is one the organisation built itself, making this outbound single-system framework mapping rather than buyer-side vetting.

intents.message: Our biggest institutional funder's reviewers asked for a structured write-up on the benefits-eligibility screener we built - how it handles each of the four risk functions in the framework they work from, where it falls short, and what we'd fix first.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the gap-and-next-steps language is scoped to one named screener mapped function by function, not to the organisation's overall posture.

intents.message: Three partners keep asking about the same tool, our volunteer-vetting model. I don't want three differently pitched notes - I want one write-up mapping that model to all four functions of the risk framework reviewers recognise.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour stakeholder-update-generator is wrong because the user explicitly rejects audience-tailored versions and wants a single four-function framework mapping of one named model.

intents.message: We already have a decent plan for when the sermon-drafting assistant goes wrong - who gets paged, how we tell people. Our accreditation reviewer wants that plan slotted in as just one quadrant of the four-function framework write-up for that assistant, with the other three filled in too.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the response plan already exists and the late clause asks for it to be absorbed into a complete four-function crosswalk of one named assistant.

intents.message: Our attendance forecasting model has drifted badly since last year and the numbers are off. I want to retrain it on the newer data and tune the hyperparameters properly - can you walk me through how to do that?
intents.notes: No skill in the set covers hands-on machine-learning engineering; retraining and hyperparameter tuning sit inside the model, whereas all twelve skills are governance, fairness, funding, decision or reporting workflows that sit around one.

intents.message: Our church office is down to two AI note-taking tools for pastoral care meetings, and the elders want a recommendation by Sunday. The feature comparison matters less to me than knowing which questions about congregants' recordings would flag a company we should walk away from.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the speaker sets aside options-and-tradeoffs framing and asks for the responsible-AI questions and red flags to put to each vendor before adopting.

intents.message: Our donor database vendor is switching on an AI feature next quarter and we have to opt in or out. I know our own internal policies are a mess, but that is a separate fight; right now I need to work out whether letting their model touch donor records is safe.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-governance-assessor is wrong because the speaker deliberately brackets their own internal posture and asks about adopting a smart feature a vendor is about to switch on.

intents.message: A fundraising platform we are considering had a public failure last year where its AI drafted a donation appeal around a statistic it invented. We have not signed anything yet, so how do I press them on that before we do?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the failure happened at a vendor the speaker has not yet bought from, and the ask is how to interrogate that vendor pre-signature rather than how to handle a future incident of their own.

intents.message: A company pitching us their volunteer-screening software says the matching engine has been checked for fairness and will not discriminate. We have not paid them a cent and I have no way to test the thing myself, so what would a credible answer to that claim even look like?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour bias-fairness-reviewer is wrong because the speaker has no access to the system to test and instead needs to judge a selling vendor's fairness claim before any purchase.

intents.message: Two of our program staff want to start on a case-note summarizer a peer organization recommended, and it is a paid subscription. Before I approve the spend I want to know what to look for in how the company uses everything we type into it.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grantee-responsible-ai-due-diligence-scorecard is wrong because the peer organization is only the source of the tip; the speaker is a buyer weighing a subscription purchase, not a funder scoring another organization.

intents.message: The AI transcription supplier we are about to sign with sent over a twelve-page conformance memo laid out against the four federal risk functions. I do not need one of those written from our side, I need to know which of their claims in it are red flags before I sign.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour nist-ai-rmf-crosswalk-generator is wrong because the speaker declines to author a crosswalk for their own system and, late in the request, asks how to read a supplier's claims for red flags ahead of signature.

intents.message: Our per-seat pricing on the volunteer database jumped forty percent at renewal and the contract has an auto-renew clause I missed. What leverage do we actually have to push this supplier back down before the January date?
intents.notes: No skill in the set claims this because it is commercial contract and price negotiation on a database with no AI component and no decision framing that any of the twelve descriptions cover.

intents.message: Same quarterly numbers, three different readers: the trustees want a page, our two funders want a couple of paragraphs, and the volunteers need it in plain language. Can you write all three so they don't contradict each other?
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the governance audience is one of three parallel versions of the same facts and nothing formal, such as motions, quorum or a packet, is requested.

intents.message: Our intake chatbot gave a family the wrong shelter address last week. We already fixed it and we already have a runbook for this kind of thing, so what I need now is the version for our board, the version for the two funders, and the version for frontline staff.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour ai-incident-response-playbook-builder is wrong because the standing process already exists and the remaining need is three audience-calibrated tellings of what happened.

intents.message: Take what I've told you about where our grants stand and give me two write-ups off the same facts, a tight one for the board and a plainer one for staff who don't follow funder jargon.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-pipeline-lifecycle-tracker is wrong because the user supplies the funding status themselves and asks only for two audience-pitched renderings of it, not for the status to be assembled or prioritized.

intents.message: This month's numbers need to reach three sets of eyes: the trustees get a page ahead of their sitting, the partner churches get three lines for their bulletin, and my staff get the whole thing. Same facts, three lengths - write each one.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour board-agenda-reporting-builder is wrong because the trustee page is one of three differently sized renderings prepared ahead of a sitting, not the packet of motions, financials and quorum handling that would constitute the sitting itself.

intents.message: Two of our funders and our lead partner each asked how the pilot is going. None of it is a required report and nothing gets submitted anywhere, so I just want one consistent set of write-ups, longer for the partner and tighter for the funders.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour grant-loi-proposal-drafter is wrong because the user rules out any submission and asks for informal, mutually consistent versions for three separate readers.

intents.message: We've already decided to close the Tuesday meal program and that call is made, so please don't re-open it. What I need is how we say it to the board, to the donors who funded it, and to the families who show up, each one honest and consistent with the others.
intents.notes: Nearest neighbour decision-brief-generator is wrong because the choice is closed and the request is three honest, mutually consistent tellings of it for different audiences.

intents.message: A reporter at the city paper covers homelessness. I'd like a press release announcing our new night shelter plus a short pitch email I could send her, both in her register rather than ours.
intents.notes: No skill in the set covers media relations, and a press release plus a journalist pitch targets one external channel rather than producing calibrated versions for the organization's own stakeholder groups.
